name: Stags' Leap Winery Petite Sirah Ne Cede Malis 2012
text:
## Stags' Leap Winery Petite Sirah Ne Cede Malis 2012

**The story.** Stags' Leap Winery lies near [Yountville](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Stags'+Leap+Winery,+Napa,+California,+USA&t=k) in the [Stags Leap District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stags_Leap_District_AVA) of [Napa Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napa_Valley_AVA). Its 240-acre estate was first planted in 1893, and its 19th-century manor house was once a bed-and-breakfast. Beringer bought it in 1997; today it belongs to [Treasury Wine Estates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treasury_Wine_Estates), owner of Penfolds ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stags'_Leap_Winery)).

**The grape: Petite Sirah.** California's Petite Sirah is mostly [Durif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durif), a cross of [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah) and the obscure Peloursin, giving tannic, spicy, plummy wines ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durif)).

**The wine: Ne Cede Malis.** "Ne cede malis" is Latin for "yield not to misfortune". Robert Whitley of Wine Review Online calls it "by far California's finest Petite for at least the past 30 years, but probably longer... nothing less than a national treasure"; fewer than 1,000 cases of the 2012 were made ([Wine Review Online](https://winereviewonline.com/?p=285622)).

**The vintage.** I couldn't read a reliable 2012 Napa vintage report, so I've left it out.

**What the critics say for 2012.**
- **Robert Whitley, Wine Review Online: 97** ([review](https://winereviewonline.com/?p=285622)). "A blockbuster that shouldn't be missed": rich and robust, blackberry, blackcurrant and dark cherry, "well proportioned yet has elegance and nuance", violets and black pepper. "A wine for the ages, unique to California, in fact unique to this particular property."
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.0** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is fourteen years old. Whitley called it a wine for the ages; at fourteen it should be softening into dark fruit, pepper and earth. Decant one to two hours ahead.

**Food.** Big, smoky food: barbecued brisket, braised short ribs, or a blue-cheese burger.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Stags' Leap Winery at the moment.

Sources:
- [Wine Review Online, Ne Cede Malis 2012](https://winereviewonline.com/?p=285622)
- [Wikipedia, Stags' Leap Winery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stags'_Leap_Winery)
